System displays an empty list with the applied filters (MSG10).
User changes the filters or the flow ends.
spec.Postconditions: No data is changed.

spec.Primary Actors: Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows executors to review the working time recorded automatically for their work items and request corrections; the Department Head applies justified corrections.
spec.Preconditions: User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
spec.Normal Flow:
Record Actual Working Time
Executor opens My Time Log.
System displays the user's work intervals for the selected day (task, cleaning, rework, incident, maintenance occurrence; start, end, duration) and the workday total (GBR-138, GBR-140).
Executor selects an interval that is wrong and selects Request Correction.
Executor enters the proposed start/end and the reason and selects Submit.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-139, GBR-012, GBR-014).
System saves the correction request as Pending and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the Department Head (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG09).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 1.1_Apply Correction
Department Head opens a Pending correction request.
System displays the original interval, proposed values and overlapping intervals.
Department Head approves (optionally adjusting values) or rejects with a reason.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-139, GBR-013, GBR-014).
System updates the interval (keeping old values) and sets the request Applied, or sets it Rejected.
System saves the decision and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the executor (GBR-010).
The flow ends.
Step 5.1_Overlap or Invalid Time
The proposed interval overlaps another or ends before it starts.
System displays MSG03 (GBR-139).
Return to step 4 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: Time records come from system events; corrections are traceable.

UC-138.name: Manage Operational Workday and Shift Records

spec.Description: Allows the Department Head to define shifts and assign employees of the department to shifts by date, for operational coordination (not payroll).
spec.Preconditions: User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
spec.Normal Flow:
Manage Operational Workday and Shift Records
Department Head opens Shifts.
System displays the shift definitions and the weekly roster of the department.
Department Head creates or edits a shift definition (code, name, start, end) or assigns employees to shifts on dates and selects Save.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-141, GBR-003, GBR-004, GBR-005).
System saves the shifts and assignments and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the affected employees (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 3.1_Cancel Assignment
Department Head removes a future assignment.
System sets it Cancelled (kept in history).
Return to step 5 of the normal flow.
Step 4.1_Overlapping Assignment
An employee would have overlapping shifts.
System displays the conflict (MSG03, GBR-141).
Return to step 3 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: Employees can start their workday for assigned shifts (UC-139). Data is not used for payroll (GBR-017).

spec.Primary Actors: Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Housekeeping Supervisor, Maintenance Lead
spec.Description: Allows an employee to record the start and end of the workday/shift; workday time is kept separate from task time recorded in UC-111.
spec.Preconditions: User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
spec.Normal Flow:
Record Workday Start and End
User selects Start Workday on the home page.
System shows today's shift assignment, if any.
User confirms.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-142).
System creates the workday with status Working and start time = server time (GBR-014).
System saves the workday and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
At the end of the shift User selects End Workday.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-143).
System sets the end time and changes the workday to Ended.
System saves the workday end and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 4.1_No Shift Assignment
User has no shift assignment today.
System asks for a reason; the workday is flagged Unscheduled and the Department Head is notified (GBR-142).
Return to step 5 of the normal flow.
Step 4.2_Already Working
User already has a Working workday.
System displays MSG03.
The flow ends.
Step 8.1_Hand Over Shift
User has open items to pass on.
System suggests UC-140 before ending the workday.
Return to step 8 of the normal flow.
Step 9.1_Open Work Item
User still has an open work interval.
System displays MSG31 and offers Pause All.
If User selects Pause All, System pauses/holds every open item with reason 'end of shift' and closes the intervals (GBR-138).
Return to step 10 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: Workday start/end are recorded; task time remains separate (GBR-140).

spec.Primary Actors: Housekeeping Supervisor, Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Lead, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows an employee ending a shift to hand over open work and notes to the next person, who acknowledges or rejects the handover.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
User has a Working workday.
spec.Normal Flow:
Manage Operational Shift Handover
User selects Shift Handover.
System prepares a snapshot of User's open items: tasks, cleaning/rework tasks, incidents, internal requests and, for leads, unready rooms (GBR-144).
User selects the receiver (an employee of the same department on the next shift), adds notes per item and general notes, and selects Submit.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-144, GBR-004).
System creates the handover as Pending Acknowledgment with the snapshot.
System saves the handover and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the receiver (GBR-010).
Receiver opens the handover, reviews the items and selects Acknowledge.
System changes the handover to Acknowledged and records the time (GBR-144).
System saves the acknowledgment and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the sender and the Department Head (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 8.1_Reject Handover
The receiver finds it incomplete.
Receiver selects Reject and enters the reason (GBR-012).
System changes the handover to Rejected and notifies the sender, who may resubmit a new version.
The flow ends.
Step 9.1_Reassign Items
A lead wants an item to be done by the receiver.
The lead uses the corresponding assign use case (UC-030, UC-053, UC-104, UC-115); the handover itself does not change assignees (GBR-144).
Return to step 10 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: The receiver is formally aware of open work; the snapshot stays unchanged.

spec.Primary Actors: Administrator, Operations Manager, Housekeeping Supervisor, Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Lead, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows an employee to send a non-material request to another department (e.g. extra towels delivered to a room, move furniture for an event, fix a lobby display) with type, priority and desired deadline.
spec.Preconditions: User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
spec.Normal Flow:
Create Internal Request
User opens Internal Requests and selects Create.
System displays the form: request type, receiving department, title, description, location (optional), priority, desired deadline, attachments.
User enters the information and selects Submit.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-145, GBR-003, GBR-004, GBR-016, GBR-014).
System creates the request with status Pending Acceptance for the receiving department.
System saves the request and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the Department Head of the receiving department (UC-124) (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG09).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 4.1_Material Need
The request type is a material need.
System advises to create a material request instead (UC-091) (MSG03, GBR-110).
The flow ends.
Step 4.1_Invalid Data
System highlights the invalid fields and shows the reason (MSG03).
Return to step 3 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: The receiving Department Head decides on the request (UC-115/UC-116).

spec.Description: Allows the receiving Department Head to route a request to the right department, or to assign/reassign the handler of an accepted request.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
User is the Department Head of the current receiving department.
spec.Normal Flow:
Route and Assign Internal Request
Department Head opens the request.
System displays the request, its history and the handlers of the department with their open requests.
Department Head selects a handler and selects Assign.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-148, GBR-004, GBR-005).
System sets the handler; an Accepted request changes to In Progress (GBR-148).
System saves the assignment and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the handler and the requester (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 3.1_Route to Another Department
The request belongs to another department and is Pending Acceptance.
Department Head selects Route, the target department and a reason (GBR-147, GBR-012).
System changes the receiving department; the request stays Pending Acceptance.
System saves the routing and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the new receiving Department Head and the requester (GBR-010).
The flow ends.
Step 4.1_Request Not Accepted Yet
The request is still Pending Acceptance.
System opens UC-116 to accept it first.
Return to step 3 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: The request has one handler responsible for it.

spec.Description: Allows the receiving Department Head to accept or reject a request, recording the reason and response time.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is Pending Acceptance and User is the Department Head of the receiving department.
spec.Normal Flow:
Accept/Reject Internal Request
Department Head opens the request.
System displays the request details and its age.
Department Head selects Accept (optionally adjusting the deadline with a reason).
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-146, GBR-014, GBR-005).
System changes the request to Accepted and records the response time.
System saves the decision and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the requester (UC-125) (GBR-010).
System offers to assign a handler (UC-115).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 3.1_Reject
The request cannot be served.
Department Head selects Reject and enters the reason (GBR-146).
System changes the request to Rejected.
System saves the decision and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the requester (GBR-010).
System displays MSG19; the flow ends.
spec.Postconditions: The request is Accepted (then assigned) or Rejected.

spec.Primary Actors: Housekeeping Supervisor, Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Lead, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows the handler to update progress, notes and results, and report issues affecting the deadline.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is In Progress and User is its handler or the receiving Department Head.
spec.Normal Flow:
Update Internal Request Progress
User opens the request and selects Update Progress.
System displays progress, notes, linked work and attachments.
User enters progress, notes or files and selects Save.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-149, GBR-050, GBR-016, GBR-005).
System saves the progress and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the requester when progress reaches 100% (ready for completion) (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 3.1_Change Deadline
The receiving Department Head changes the deadline.
Department Head enters the new deadline and reason (GBR-149).
Return to step 4 of the normal flow.
Step 4.1_Not Allowed to Change Deadline
A handler who is not the Department Head changes the deadline.
System displays MSG02.
Return to step 3 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: Progress is visible to the requester; the request stays In Progress.

spec.Description: Allows the receiving side to create or link the operational work needed to fulfil a request (cleaning task, incident, material request or operational task).
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is Accepted or In Progress.
spec.Normal Flow:
Create Linked Operational Work
User opens the request and selects Linked Work.
System displays linked records and the options Link Existing or Create New (cleaning task, incident, material request, operational task).
User selects Create New and the record type.
System opens the target use case (UC-028, UC-049, UC-091 or UC-102) prefilled from the request; permissions of that use case apply (GBR-150, GBR-002).
After the record is saved, System links it to the request and marks whether it is mandatory for completion.
System saves the link and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 3.1_Link Existing Record
User selects Link Existing.
System lists open records of the selected type in the branch that User can view.
User selects one; return to Step 6.
Step 4.1_No Permission for Target
User lacks the permission of the target use case (e.g. a Department Head creating a cleaning task).
System displays MSG02 and suggests linking an existing record or asking the responsible role (GBR-150).
Return to step 2 of the normal flow.
spec.Postconditions: Linked work is traceable from the request; the request is not closed automatically.

spec.Primary Actors: Housekeeping Supervisor, Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Lead, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows the current handler to hand over a request to another handler (staff change or shift change); responsibility moves only after acknowledgment.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is In Progress and User is its handler.
spec.Normal Flow:
Record Request Handover
Handler opens the request and selects Hand Over.
System displays eligible handlers of the receiving department.
Handler selects the new handler, enters the status summary and notes and selects Submit.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-151, GBR-004).
System creates a handover Pending Acknowledgment; the current handler stays responsible (GBR-151).
System saves the handover and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the designated new handler (GBR-010).
New handler opens the handover and selects Acknowledge.
System changes the handover to Acknowledged and sets the new handler on the request.
System saves the acknowledgment and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the previous handler and the receiving Department Head (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 8.1_Reject Handover
The new handler cannot take it.
New handler selects Reject with a reason; System sets the handover Rejected; the previous handler remains (GBR-151).
The flow ends.
spec.Postconditions: The request always has exactly one responsible handler.

spec.Description: Allows the receiving Department Head to confirm that a request is fulfilled, record the result and close it.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is In Progress.
spec.Normal Flow:
Complete Internal Request
Department Head opens the request and selects Complete.
System displays linked work with statuses and pending handovers.
Department Head enters the result note and selects Close.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-152, GBR-003, GBR-005).
System changes the request from In Progress to Closed and closes its Open escalation, if any.
System saves the closure and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the requester (UC-125) (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 4.1_Open Mandatory Work or Pending Handover
Linked mandatory work is not closed or a handover is pending.
System lists them (MSG34, GBR-152).
The flow ends.
spec.Postconditions: The request is Closed; the requester may reopen it within SYS-PAR-18 days.

spec.Primary Actors: Administrator, Operations Manager, Housekeeping Supervisor, Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Lead, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows the requester (or the requesting Department Head) to reopen a closed request when the result is unsatisfactory.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is Closed and User is its requester or the Department Head of the requesting department.
spec.Normal Flow:
Reopen Internal Request
User opens the request and selects Reopen.
System displays the result and the reopen window (GBR-153).
User enters what is unsatisfactory and selects Reopen.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-153, GBR-012).
System changes the request from Closed to In Progress with the last handler; previous results and handovers are kept.
System saves the reopening and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the handler and the receiving Department Head (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 4.1_Window Expired
The request was closed more than SYS-PAR-18 days ago.
System displays MSG03 and suggests a new request (UC-114).
The flow ends.
spec.Postconditions: The request is In Progress again.

spec.Description: Allows the Operations Manager to intervene on an overdue or at-risk request: change priority or deadline, reroute it or change its handler.
spec.Preconditions:
User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
The request is not Closed, Rejected or Cancelled and is overdue or at risk (GBR-156).
spec.Normal Flow:
Escalate Overdue Internal Request
Operations Manager opens Overdue Requests (or the overdue alert) and selects a request.
System displays age, deadline, handler, progress and history.
Operations Manager selects Escalate and enters the action: new priority, new deadline, new receiving department or new handler, plus the reason.
System validates the input and business conditions (GBR-155, GBR-012, GBR-005).
System creates an Open escalation and applies the selected changes.
System saves the escalation and changes and records the audit log in the same transaction (GBR-007, GBR-008).
System sends an in-app notification to the requester, the receiving Department Head and the handler; the alert requires acknowledgment (GBR-010).
System displays a success message (MSG08).
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 4.1_Not Eligible or Already Escalated
The request is not overdue/at risk or already has an Open escalation.
System displays MSG03 (GBR-155).
The flow ends.
spec.Postconditions: The escalation is closed automatically when the request is closed.

spec.Primary Actors: Administrator, Operations Manager, Housekeeping Supervisor, Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Lead, Maintenance Staff, Storekeeper, Department Head
spec.Description: Allows users to look up internal requests they sent, received or handle, with status, handler, deadline, history and results; the requester can withdraw a request not yet accepted.
spec.Preconditions: User has logged in and has permission for this function (GBR-001, GBR-002).
spec.Normal Flow:
View Internal Request History
User opens the Internal Requests screen.
System displays requests visible to the user with status, receiving department, handler, deadline and overdue flag (GBR-156), sorted by deadline (GBR-015).
User filters by direction (sent/received), status, type, priority, department and overdue flag or searches by keyword.
System refreshes the list with matching records in the user's scope (GBR-015).
User selects a request.
System displays the timeline: routing, decisions, handlers, handovers, progress, linked work (only records User may view), escalations and result.
spec.Alternative Flows:
Step 4.1_No Matching Records
No record matches the filters.
System displays an empty list with the applied filters (MSG10).
User changes the filters or the flow ends.
Step 5.1_Withdraw Request

rules.GBR-001: Every request except Login and Forgot Password requires a valid, unexpired and unrevoked session.
rules.GBR-002: A user may perform a UC only when one of the user's active roles grants the UC permission (Permission Matrix 4.4) and the target record belongs to the user's assigned branch/department scope. A user may hold several roles; effective permissions are the union of the roles' grants, limited by scope.
rules.GBR-003: Mandatory fields must not be empty; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed from codes and names; codes are compared case-insensitively.
rules.GBR-004: Every referenced record must exist within the user's scope; records selected for a new business operation must be Active.
rules.GBR-005: An update is accepted only if the record's row_version equals the version the user loaded; otherwise the update is rejected and the user must reload.
rules.GBR-006: Actions that post, approve, complete or hand over re-check the record's current status inside the same transaction; a repeated submission (double click or retry) of an action already processed is rejected and the current result is shown.
rules.GBR-007: A business operation, its status changes, stock ledger entries, room status recalculation and audit record are saved in one transaction; if any part fails nothing is saved.
rules.GBR-008: Every create, update, status change, approval, posting, reversal, permission change and login/logout is recorded in the audit log with actor, time (UTC), entity, action and before/after values. Passwords, password hashes and tokens are never recorded.
rules.GBR-009: Master data and business records that have been referenced are never physically deleted; they are deactivated, cancelled or reversed, and their history remains viewable.
rules.GBR-010: Each committed business event creates at most one in-app notification per recipient, who must have read permission on the source record. If a notification cannot be created, the business operation is still kept and the notification job retries it.
rules.GBR-011: Reading or acknowledging a notification never approves, accepts, closes or changes the source record.
rules.GBR-012: Cancellation, rejection, reversal, reopening, deactivation and manual overrides require a reason of at least 10 characters.
rules.GBR-013: The user who approves, verifies or concludes a result must not be the requester, submitter or performer of the same processing cycle. Each cycle stores submitted_by, performed_by and verified_by.
rules.GBR-014: All timestamps are generated by the server, stored in UTC and displayed/calculated in SYS-PAR-10. An end time must not be earlier than its start time; a deadline must not be earlier than its planned start.
rules.GBR-015: Lists are paginated (default SYS-PAR-11), sorted by the UC's default order with the record ID as tie-breaker, and only contain records in the user's scope. A date range end must not precede its start.
rules.GBR-016: Attachments must have an allowed format (SYS-PAR-07), at most SYS-PAR-08 MB per file and SYS-PAR-09 files per upload, and must be fully uploaded before the record is saved. Files are stored privately and every download re-checks permission on the source record.
rules.GBR-017: HotelOps V1 does not handle reservations, room sales, check-in/check-out, guest payment, OTA, accounting, payroll or purchasing approval. PMS integration is optional and not required in V1.
rules.GBR-018: Department Head is the head of any department (including Housekeeping, Maintenance and Warehouse). A user may additionally hold Housekeeping Supervisor or Maintenance Lead roles; such a user is still subject to segregation of duties.
rules.GBR-019: Login accepts a username or email with a password. Wrong password, unknown account and Inactive account all return the same message (MSG11) so that account existence is not disclosed.
rules.GBR-020: After SYS-PAR-01 consecutive failed attempts the account is locked until now + SYS-PAR-02 minutes (locked_until). A successful login resets the counter. While locked, a correct password returns MSG12; an incorrect password returns MSG11.
rules.GBR-021: A session expires after SYS-PAR-06 minutes without activity; each valid request extends it. Logout and password change revoke the session(s).
rules.GBR-022: A password must have at least SYS-PAR-03 characters and contain an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character (SYS-PAR-04), and must differ from the current password.
rules.GBR-023: New accounts and credential resets receive a random temporary password shown once to the Administrator and valid for SYS-PAR-05 hours. A session created with a temporary password can only change the password; all other functions are blocked until it is changed.
rules.GBR-024: Forgot Password never reveals whether an account exists; it always shows MSG14 and the user contacts the Administrator, who resets the credential in UC-005.
rules.GBR-025: Username and email are unique across the whole system.
rules.GBR-026: At least one Active account must keep an active Administrator role with permission administration; deactivating, revoking or reconfiguring that would remove the last one is rejected.
rules.GBR-027: An Administrator cannot deactivate their own account or revoke their own Administrator role.
rules.GBR-028: An account with open assigned work (tasks, cleaning, rework, incidents, internal requests) can be deactivated or moved to another scope only after that work has been reassigned or handed over.
rules.GBR-029: Role code is unique; system roles (the nine actors) cannot be deleted, only their permissions adjusted.
rules.GBR-030: Permissions are chosen only from the system permission list (one permission per use case, see 4.4); granting a permission does not bypass scope or segregation-of-duty rules.
rules.GBR-031: A user is assigned to one or more branches; within a branch, to one or more departments. The department must belong to the branch. Owner and Operations Manager may be assigned to several branches.
rules.GBR-032: Branch code is unique; branch name and address are mandatory. All branches use the system timezone SYS-PAR-10.
rules.GBR-033: A branch can be deactivated only when it has no active rooms, warehouses with stock, open tasks, open incidents or open requests.
rules.GBR-034: Floor/area code is unique within its branch; an area may belong to a floor of the same branch; the parent chain must not form a cycle.
rules.GBR-035: A floor/area can be deactivated only when it has no active rooms, active child areas, active assets or open incidents/tasks located there.
rules.GBR-036: Room type code is unique within the branch; room type attributes are used only for operations (cleaning standard, default checklist), never for pricing.
rules.GBR-037: A room type can be deactivated only when no active room uses it.
rules.GBR-038: Room number is unique within the branch; the room's floor and room type must be active and belong to the same branch.
rules.GBR-039: A newly created room starts with operational status Pending Cleaning; it can only become Ready through a passed inspection.
rules.GBR-040: A room can be deactivated only when it has no open cleaning task, rework, inspection, incident or effective block; its assets must be moved first.
rules.GBR-041: Department code is unique within the branch; a department may have one Department Head user.
rules.GBR-042: A department can be deactivated only when it has no active users, warehouses, open tasks, open internal requests or assets in custody.
rules.GBR-043: Room operational status is calculated by the system, never typed by users. It is recalculated in the same transaction as every source event (cleaning, inspection, rework, block, room activation) and each change is stored in room status history with old/new status, source event and time.
rules.GBR-044: Room status is the first matching condition: (1) Inactive if the room is inactive; (2) Blocked if it has at least one effective block; (3) Rework Required if the current cleaning cycle needs rework that is not yet submitted; (4) Cleaning In Progress if its cleaning task is In Progress; (5) Pending Cleaning if its cleaning task is Pending Assignment, Assigned or On Hold, or the room has never passed inspection; (6) Pending Inspection if cleaning or rework has been submitted and awaits inspection; (7) Ready if the latest cleaning cycle is Completed. Cancelled cleaning tasks are ignored.
rules.GBR-045: A room may have only one open cleaning task (any status other than Completed or Cancelled).
rules.GBR-046: A cleaning or rework task can be assigned only to an Active user holding the Housekeeping Staff role in the room's branch and Housekeeping department.
rules.GBR-047: Reassignment is allowed while the cleaning task is Assigned, In Progress or On Hold; the previous assignee's open work interval is closed at the reassignment time and the task returns to Assigned.
rules.GBR-048: Only a Housekeeping Supervisor can cancel a cleaning task, and only while it is Pending Assignment or Assigned (no work started). Cancelled tasks remain in history.
rules.GBR-049: Only the current assignee can start or resume a cleaning task, and only from Assigned or On Hold.
rules.GBR-050: Progress is 0 to 100 percent; reaching 100 does not complete the task.
rules.GBR-051: Reporting a blocker puts the cleaning task On Hold, closes the assignee's open work interval and notifies the Housekeeping Supervisor. The same open blocker reason cannot be reported twice for one task.
rules.GBR-052: A cleaning task can be completed only from In Progress, when all mandatory cleaning items are ticked and no blocker is open; it then becomes Pending Inspection.
rules.GBR-053: Only the assigned Housekeeping Staff can accept and start a rework task; acceptance is from Pending Acceptance, start is from Accepted.
rules.GBR-054: A rework task can be submitted only from In Progress and only when every defect listed in it has a remediation note; it then becomes Pending Reinspection.
rules.GBR-055: A cleaning or rework task is overdue when it is not Completed/Cancelled and the current time is after its due time.
rules.GBR-056: A checklist has at least one criterion; each criterion states whether it is mandatory. Only a Published checklist version can be used for inspections.
rules.GBR-057: A checklist version that has been used by an inspection is never edited; changes create a new version, and the previous version is Retired. Past inspections always show the version they used.
rules.GBR-058: An inspection can be assigned only for a room whose cleaning task is Pending Inspection (or whose rework is Pending Reinspection), to an Active user with the Housekeeping Supervisor role; one open inspection per cleaning cycle.
rules.GBR-059: The inspector must not be the person who performed the cleaning or rework being inspected.
rules.GBR-060: Only the assigned inspector can record results; every mandatory criterion must have a Pass/Fail result, and each Fail must have at least one defect with a description before the inspection can be concluded.
rules.GBR-061: Defects can be added or changed only while the inspection is Inspecting or Pending Conclusion; they are locked after the conclusion.
rules.GBR-062: An inspection can be concluded Passed only when all mandatory criteria are Pass. Passing sets the cleaning task Completed; the room becomes Ready unless it has an effective block (MSG17).
rules.GBR-063: An inspection concluded Failed sets the cleaning task to Rework Required and the room to Rework Required (unless Blocked). A rework request must then be created.
rules.GBR-064: A rework task is created from a Failed inspection with the defects to fix, a due time and an assignee; one open rework task per inspection.
rules.GBR-065: A reinspection checks every defect of the rework task and is linked to the original inspection. If all are fixed, the rework task, the reinspection and the cleaning task are completed; otherwise the rework task becomes Failed and a new rework task must be requested.
rules.GBR-066: An incident must have a branch and at least one of room, area or asset; an asset must belong to the selected branch.
rules.GBR-067: Before saving a new incident the system shows open incidents at the same room/area/asset; the reporter may add evidence to an existing one instead.
rules.GBR-068: Category and severity (Low, Normal, High, Critical) must be set before triage. Severity Critical immediately alerts the Maintenance Lead and Operations Manager.
rules.GBR-069: Triage is done only on Pending Triage incidents and sets priority, response deadline and resolution deadline. Default deadlines are calculated from detected time and the SLA targets of the priority (reference data); changing them requires a reason.
rules.GBR-070: An incident can be cancelled as Duplicate or Invalid only while Pending Triage; a duplicate must reference the original incident.
rules.GBR-071: Maintenance work can be assigned or reassigned only when the incident is Pending Assignment or Assigned, to an Active Maintenance Staff or Maintenance Lead in the incident's branch. A Maintenance Lead may be assigned only if another active Maintenance Lead of the branch can verify the result.
rules.GBR-072: Only the assignee can accept and start the work, from Assigned; acceptance time is the response time used for SLA.
rules.GBR-073: The assignee can put an In Progress incident On Hold with a reason (e.g. waiting for materials) and resume it later; holding closes the open work interval. SLA time is not paused.
rules.GBR-074: Materials recorded as used on an incident must come from material issues linked to that incident and cannot exceed the issued quantity not yet returned.
rules.GBR-075: A room block links one incident to one room; each incident-room pair has at most one effective block. A block can be removed early by the Maintenance Lead with a reason, and is removed automatically when the incident is closed or cancelled.
rules.GBR-076: An incident can be escalated to the Operations Manager when its severity is Critical or it is at risk (SYS-PAR-21 of the resolution time used) or overdue; only one Open escalation per incident.
rules.GBR-077: Resolution results (diagnosis, action taken, actual end time) can be submitted only by the assignee from In Progress; the incident becomes Pending Verification and the work interval is closed.
rules.GBR-078: Only Pending Verification incidents can be verified. The verifier is a Maintenance Lead of the branch who did not submit or perform the work. Returning results sends the incident back to In Progress with a reason.
rules.GBR-079: A Closed incident can be reopened within SYS-PAR-19 days with a reason; it returns to Pending Triage as a new processing cycle and previous cycles are kept.
rules.GBR-080: An incident is overdue when it is not Closed/Cancelled and now is after its resolution deadline; response is overdue when it has not been accepted by the response deadline.
rules.GBR-081: A preventive maintenance schedule targets one asset, room or area, has an interval greater than 0 (days, weeks or months), a first due date and a work description; an object cannot have two Active schedules with the same title.
rules.GBR-082: Editing a schedule affects only future occurrences; deactivating it does not cancel occurrences already generated.
rules.GBR-083: The system generates a maintenance occurrence SYS-PAR-16 days before each due date; it is Assigned to the schedule's default assignee or Pending Assignment if none. The next due date is calculated from the scheduled due date, not from the completion date.
rules.GBR-084: Only the assignee can start and complete an occurrence; every mandatory check item needs a result. Problems found are reported as new incidents linked to the occurrence.
rules.GBR-085: Reference codes (task categories, incident categories, blocker/pause reasons, request types, cleaning types, priorities) are unique within their group; used values can only be deactivated and keep their meaning in history. Priority codes LOW, NORMAL, HIGH, CRITICAL are fixed; only their labels and SLA targets can be changed.
rules.GBR-086: Asset code is unique; an asset belongs to one branch, one category and has exactly one current location (room or area) and one custodian department at a time.
rules.GBR-087: A location change is recorded as a movement with old/new location, time, actor and reason; transferring to another branch requires scope in both branches. An asset with an open incident or maintenance occurrence needs a confirmation note before moving.
rules.GBR-088: A custody handover moves responsibility only when the designated receiver (Department Head of the receiving department) acknowledges it; until then the sender remains responsible. A rejected handover needs a reason and may be resubmitted as a new version.
rules.GBR-089: Asset condition is In Use, Damaged or Under Repair. Setting In Use after Damaged/Under Repair requires that linked incidents are Closed or a reason is given.
rules.GBR-090: An asset can be retired only when it has no open incident, open maintenance occurrence, active schedule or pending handover; retired assets are excluded from active statistics but keep their history.
rules.GBR-091: Warehouse code is unique within the branch; a warehouse belongs to one branch and one responsible department. A warehouse can be deactivated only when all balances are zero and it has no Draft, In Transit or Partially Received documents.
rules.GBR-092: Item code is unique; each item has one base unit that cannot change after the first stock transaction.
rules.GBR-093: Each additional unit of an item has exactly one positive conversion factor to the base unit. All stock quantities are stored in the base unit and documents keep the factor used.
rules.GBR-094: Minimum stock level is ≥ 0 and set per warehouse and item; items without a minimum never raise low-stock alerts.
rules.GBR-095: Requested, received, issued, transferred and returned quantities must be greater than 0; counted quantities must be ≥ 0.
rules.GBR-096: Only Posted (or dispatched/received transfer) documents change stock; drafts, requests and approvals never change stock.
rules.GBR-097: Available stock of a warehouse/item must never become negative after an issue, transfer dispatch, adjustment or reversal.
rules.GBR-098: A Posted document is never edited or deleted; corrections are made only by reversal (UC-088) or adjustment (UC-087).
rules.GBR-099: A receipt has at least one line. When posting, the received quantity of each line is entered; a difference from the expected quantity needs a reason. Rejected (damaged) quantities do not increase stock.
rules.GBR-100: A Draft receipt can be edited or cancelled (with reason) by a Storekeeper; a Cancelled receipt never changes stock.
rules.GBR-101: Every stock issue to a department is linked to an Approved or Partially Issued material request line, and the issued quantity cannot exceed that line's remaining approved quantity.
rules.GBR-102: A return refers to a previous issue; the cumulative returned quantity cannot exceed the issued quantity. Only quantities accepted as usable increase stock; damaged quantities are recorded with a reason. Returns do not restore the request's approved quantity.
rules.GBR-103: Source and destination warehouses differ. Dispatch requires sufficient source stock and moves the quantity out of the source into in-transit in one transaction.
rules.GBR-104: The destination confirms received, damaged and missing quantities per line, possibly in several batches; their total cannot exceed the dispatched quantity not yet confirmed. The transfer is Received when everything dispatched is confirmed, otherwise Partially Received. Damaged and missing quantities need a reason and are reported as transfer losses.
rules.GBR-105: A stocktake fixes a cutoff time for one warehouse; system quantities are the balances at the cutoff, and movements after the cutoff are excluded. Only one open stocktake per warehouse.
rules.GBR-106: Discrepancy = counted quantity − system quantity at cutoff; every non-zero discrepancy needs a cause. A stocktake without discrepancies is Reconciled without an adjustment.
rules.GBR-107: An adjustment is posted only by the Operations Manager, based on a Pending Adjustment stocktake or an error-correction reason; a stocktake can be the basis of only one adjustment.
rules.GBR-108: Only Posted receipts, issues, returns and adjustments can be reversed, once, by the Operations Manager, by creating an offsetting document. A reversal is rejected if it would make stock negative or if later dependent documents (e.g. returns of the reversed issue) exist; reversing an issue reduces the request's issued quantity.
rules.GBR-109: The stock ledger lists only posted movements; balance at a date = sum of posted movements up to that date. No movement in a period does not mean zero balance.
rules.GBR-110: A material request has at least one line (item, quantity, unit), a purpose, a receiving department/location and a needed-by time. Material needs must use a material request, not an internal request.
rules.GBR-111: The approver is the Department Head of the requester's department; when the requester is that Department Head, the approver is the Department Head of the department responsible for the issuing warehouse. The approver must always differ from the requester.
rules.GBR-112: Only the creator can edit a request while Draft, Pending Approval or Needs Information. Editing an Approved request that has nothing issued returns it to Pending Approval and clears approved quantities.
rules.GBR-113: Only the creator can cancel a request with nothing issued (Draft, Pending Approval, Needs Information or Approved). A Partially Issued request cannot be cancelled; its remainder can be closed by the approver.
rules.GBR-114: Reviewing a request does not reserve stock. The approver may return it for more information; the creator then edits and resubmits it.
rules.GBR-115: Approval is only from Pending Approval; each approved quantity is between 0 and the requested quantity and at least one line must be greater than 0; approving all lines with 0 is a rejection. Rejection needs a reason.
rules.GBR-116: Fulfillable quantity = min(available stock, remaining approved quantity). Issuing the whole remainder sets Fully Issued; issuing less sets Partially Issued and keeps the remainder open.
rules.GBR-117: The approver can close the unissued remainder of a Partially Issued request with a reason; issued quantities are unchanged.
rules.GBR-118: A request can be linked only to an open work record (cleaning task, incident, maintenance occurrence or operational task) of the same branch; Cancelled or Rejected requests cannot be linked.
rules.GBR-119: A user can view requests they created, requests of their department (Department Head), requests they approve, and requests to fulfil (Storekeeper); Operations Manager sees all in scope.
rules.GBR-120: A replenishment request is created for items below minimum stock or for shortages of approved material requests; it has lines (item, unit, quantity), the receiving warehouse and optional supplier name and expected date. The same shortage cannot be requested twice in open replenishments.
rules.GBR-121: Received quantities of a replenishment come only from Posted receipts linked to it; each receipt line counts once. Status becomes Partially Received or Fully Received automatically.
rules.GBR-122: An open replenishment can be closed by the Storekeeper with a reason when the remaining quantity will not arrive.
rules.GBR-123: An operational task has a title, category, location or department, expected outcome and at least one completion criterion. A need that has a specialised process (cleaning, incident, material) must use that process instead.
rules.GBR-124: A recurring task series defines a rule (daily, weekly on chosen days, or monthly on a day), a default assignee and an end date (optional). The system creates each occurrence SYS-PAR-17 days before it is due; deactivating the series stops future occurrences only.
rules.GBR-125: Priority is Low, Normal, High or Critical. Changing a deadline after assignment requires a reason and keeps the previous deadline in history.
rules.GBR-126: A task is assigned only to an Active user holding an executor role (Housekeeping Staff, Maintenance Staff or Storekeeper) in the task's department and branch.
rules.GBR-127: Reassignment is allowed before the task is Pending Verification; the previous assignee's open work interval is closed and the task returns to Assigned for the new assignee.
rules.GBR-128: A task can be cancelled by the Department Head only while it has no recorded work time (Pending Assignment, Assigned or Accepted).
rules.GBR-129: Only the assignee can accept or decline an Assigned task; declining requires a reason and returns it to Pending Assignment.
rules.GBR-130: Only the assignee can start an Accepted task or resume a Paused task.
rules.GBR-131: Only In Progress tasks can be paused, with a pause reason; pausing closes the work interval.
rules.GBR-132: A task can be submitted only from In Progress by the assignee, when every mandatory completion criterion has a result; it becomes Pending Verification.
rules.GBR-133: The Department Head verifies Pending Verification tasks: Accept closes the task; Return requires a reason and sends it back to Accepted for the same assignee.
rules.GBR-134: A Closed task can be reopened by the Department Head with a reason and remediation instructions; it becomes Assigned (same or new assignee) as a new cycle.
rules.GBR-135: A task is overdue when it is not Closed/Cancelled and now is after its deadline.
rules.GBR-136: A user must have a Working workday before starting or resuming any work item (cleaning, rework, maintenance, occurrence, task).
rules.GBR-137: A user has at most one open work interval at any time; to start another work item the current one must be paused, put on hold or completed.
rules.GBR-138: Work intervals are opened and closed automatically by start/resume and pause/hold/complete/reassign events, using server time. Users cannot type or back-date intervals.
rules.GBR-139: An executor can request a correction of their own interval with a reason; only a Department Head with the work_interval.correct permission applies it. The change keeps old and new values, must not create overlaps and is audited.
rules.GBR-140: Task effort = sum of closed work intervals of the task; open intervals are shown separately as provisional; shift duration never replaces task time.
rules.GBR-141: Shift definitions have a code, start and end time; an employee cannot have overlapping shift assignments. Shifts are for operational coordination only, not attendance or payroll.
rules.GBR-142: A user can start a workday when assigned to a shift for that date; starting without an assignment requires a reason and notifies the Department Head. A user cannot have two Working workdays.
rules.GBR-143: A workday can be ended only when the user has no open work interval; the user may choose to pause all open work items first.
rules.GBR-144: A shift handover snapshots the sender's open items (tasks, cleaning, incidents, internal requests, unready rooms) and notes at submission time. Acknowledgment by the receiver confirms awareness; reassignment of individual items is still done through the corresponding assign UCs.
rules.GBR-145: An internal request has a request type, receiving department, title, description, priority and desired deadline; the receiving department must be active.
rules.GBR-146: Only the Department Head of the current receiving department can accept, reject or route a Pending Acceptance request; rejection needs a reason.
rules.GBR-147: Routing changes the receiving department; the request stays Pending Acceptance and the previous department keeps no responsibility.
rules.GBR-148: An Accepted or In Progress request is assigned to a handler of the receiving department; the first assignment moves it to In Progress.
rules.GBR-149: Only the current handler (or the receiving Department Head) can update progress; progress 0–100 does not close the request; only the Department Head can change the deadline, with a reason.
rules.GBR-150: Work created from a request uses the target process and its permissions (UC-028 for cleaning, UC-049 for incidents, UC-091 for materials, UC-102 for tasks); creating linked work does not close the request.
rules.GBR-151: A handler handover becomes effective only when the designated new handler acknowledges it; until then the sender remains the handler.
rules.GBR-152: A request can be completed only when all mandatory linked work is closed and no handover is pending; the result note is mandatory.
rules.GBR-153: The requester (or requesting Department Head) can reopen a Closed request within SYS-PAR-18 days with a reason; it returns to In Progress with the last handler.
rules.GBR-154: The requester can withdraw a request only while it is Pending Acceptance; it becomes Cancelled.
rules.GBR-155: An overdue or at-risk (SYS-PAR-21) request can be escalated by the Operations Manager, who may change priority, deadline, receiving department or handler; one Open escalation per request.
rules.GBR-156: An internal request is overdue when it is not Closed/Rejected/Cancelled and now is after its deadline.
rules.GBR-157: Users see only notifications addressed to them; opening a notification re-checks permission on the source record.
rules.GBR-158: Overdue and low-stock alerts are checked every SYS-PAR-15 minutes and sent once per violation episode; a new alert is sent only after the condition has ended and occurred again.
rules.GBR-159: Marking read sets read time once; acknowledging is required for Critical incident alerts and escalations and records the acknowledgment time once.
rules.GBR-160: Notifications are kept for SYS-PAR-14 days.
rules.GBR-161: A dashboard or report uses one snapshot time for all figures, counts each record once by ID, shows its filters and snapshot time, never treats missing data as 0, and shows N/A when a denominator is 0. Period figures default to the last SYS-PAR-20 days.
rules.GBR-162: Dashboards and reports are available to the Operations Manager and the Owner only, limited to the branches in their scope.
rules.GBR-163: Preview and export use the same filters and snapshot; exports are CSV, XLSX or PDF, contain only permitted fields and at most SYS-PAR-12 data rows (larger results are refused, never truncated).
rules.GBR-164: Audit records are append-only, read-only for everyone and kept for SYS-PAR-13 days.
